title: The Heaviest Spider Is Named for a Meal It Almost Never Eats
subject: goliath birdeater

scenes.text: The heaviest spider on Earth is named after a meal it almost never eats.
The goliath birdeater weighs about 170 grams and spans eleven inches. Its fangs are over an inch long.
So why the name? An old engraving showed a different tarantula eating a hummingbird. The label stuck.
Its real menu is worms, frogs, mice, lizards, even snakes. Birds are rare.
Threatened, it rubs its legs together and hisses loud enough to hear from fifteen feet away.
Then it flicks barbed hairs at your eyes. The birdeater barely eats birds.

description:
The goliath birdeater is the heaviest spider known, yet it almost never eats birds.
The name comes from an old engraving of a different tarantula with a hummingbird. Its real diet is worms, insects, frogs, mice, lizards and snakes, and when threatened it hisses by rubbing its legs together and flicks irritating hairs at attackers.
Would you hold one? Tell us below.
first_comment: Its barbed hairs can irritate skin and eyes for days. Would you keep one as a pet, or is this where you draw the line?
